review_artifact.root_cause: The GET /books/<int:book_id> handler serialized the result of BOOKS.get(book_id) unconditionally. For an absent ID, None became JSON null and Flask returned its default HTTP 200 status.
review_artifact.behavior_fixed: The handler now returns HTTP 404 with {"error":"book not found"} when the lookup returns None, while preserving the existing HTTP 200 response and JSON contract for known books.

verification_performed.description: Compared the resulting app tree with the pristine reference and inspected the source diff.
Ran the visible pytest suite with capture and cache disabled in the read-only verifier environment.
Used Flask's test client to check existing IDs 1 and 2 and missing ID 999, including status codes, JSON bodies, and content type.

verification_results.result: The only intentional source change is a two-line missing-book branch in app/main.py; generated Python bytecode was also present as a non-source artifact.
Passed: 1 visible test passed in 0.61 seconds, confirming the existing-book response remains unchanged.

Passed: /books/1 and /books/2 returned HTTP 200 with their original JSON objects; /books/999 returned HTTP 404 with {"error":"book not found"}; all responses were application/json. The independent verifier passed the repair.

review_artifact.remaining_risk: Hidden evaluation has not run. The public contract covers missing integer IDs; malformed or non-integer paths still use Flask's routing-level 404 response. Generated __pycache__ files are present but do not alter production source behavior.
